subject.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback

question: Should routine security audit and Doctor lint warn when `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` intentionally wins over a configured gateway token SecretRef, and should that supported precedence make Doctor lint return unsuccessful?
rationale: Current documentation defines the environment token as the winning auth input in this state, while the PR intentionally reframes it as a security fallback warning; severity and lint failure semantics are product security policy rather than a mechanically resolvable code defect.

options.title: Warn only on unexpected fallback
options.body: Treat documented intentional environment precedence as informational and reserve warnings or lint failure for an active SecretRef that was actually attempted and unexpectedly fell back.

options.title: Adopt the current warning policy
options.body: Treat every configured SecretRef displaced by environment credentials as an actionable security warning and accept the resulting Doctor lint compatibility change.

options.title: Limit the PR to plugin paths
options.body: Land the objective plugin filesystem diagnostics now and defer SecretRef fallback policy to a separately reviewed security change.

recommendation.title: Warn only on unexpected fallback
recommendation.body: Treat documented intentional environment precedence as informational and reserve warnings or lint failure for an active SecretRef that was actually attempted and unexpectedly fell back.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sets gateway-auth security posture and operator-facing compatibility semantics across audit and Doctor.
